title: Hom-product image stabilization gives uniform transition factorizations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and $(M_i,f_{ij})_{i\in I}$ a directed system of $R$-modules, so $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ik}=f_{jk}\circ f_{ij}$ whenever $i\le j\le k$. Put $P=\prod_{s\in I}M_s$, the module of all families with componentwise operations. Suppose that for every $i\in I$ there is $j\ge i$ such that for every $k\ge j$ the images of the precomposition maps $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,P)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,P)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_k,P)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,P)$ are equal. Then for every $i\in I$ there is $j\ge i$ such that for every $k\ge i$ there is an $R$-linear map $h_{i,k}:M_k\to M_j$ with $f_{ij}=h_{i,k}\circ f_{ik}$. No finite-presentation or countability assumption on the modules or on $I$ is imposed. A directed system is regarded as a diagram in the category of modules, in the terminology of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (5) implies (3); the proof uses only the displayed Hom-image hypothesis and directed-system identities, without the finite-presentation assumptions of the surrounding proposition.

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$ and choose $j\ge i$ from the image-stabilization hypothesis. Define $e_j:M_j\to P$ by $(e_j(x))_s=x$ when $s=j$, and $0\in M_s$ otherwise; define $\pi_j:P\to M_j$ by $\pi_j((x_s)_s)=x_j$. Both maps preserve addition and scalar multiplication coordinatewise: at $s=j$ the required identities are those in $M_j$, and elsewhere they are $0+0=0$ and $r0=0$. Thus they are $R$-linear and $\pi_j\circ e_j=\mathrm{id}_{M_j}$.

For any $\ell\ge j$, the map $e_j\circ f_{ij}:M_i\to P$ lies in the image of precomposition from $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_j,P)$, witnessed by $e_j$. The assumed equality of images therefore gives an $R$-linear map $a_\ell:M_\ell\to P$ with $a_\ell\circ f_{i\ell}=e_j\circ f_{ij}$. Set $g_\ell=\pi_j\circ a_\ell:M_\ell\to M_j$. Composition preserves linearity directly, and $g_\ell\circ f_{i\ell}=\pi_j\circ e_j\circ f_{ij}=f_{ij}$.

Now let $k\ge i$ be arbitrary. Directedness gives $\ell\in I$ with $\ell\ge j$ and $\ell\ge k$. Apply Step 2 at $\ell$ and put $h_{i,k}=g_\ell\circ f_{k\ell}:M_k\to M_j$. This map is $R$-linear, and the directed-system identity gives $h_{i,k}\circ f_{ik}=g_\ell\circ f_{k\ell}\circ f_{ik}=g_\ell\circ f_{i\ell}=f_{ij}$. The same $j$ works for every $k\ge i$, including $k$ incomparable with $j$. Only the stated image equality, coordinatewise module operations, directedness and the transition identities were used; finite presentation and countability are unnecessary.

Step 1 defines the coordinate insertion e_j and projection pi_j and checks pi_j e_j = id; this is elementary. Step 2: for l >= j, the map e_j f_ij lies in the image from Hom(M_j,P), so the stated image equality (used only for l >= j) gives a_l, and g_l = pi_j a_l satisfies g_l f_il = f_ij. Step 3: for any k >= i, a common upper bound l >= j,k gives h = g_l f_kl, and the transition identity f_kl f_ik = f_il holds since i <= k <= l. This also covers k incomparable with j, a case the source's last sentence leaves out. Marking all steps elementary is justified (C1/C2 fine) and proof_deps = [] is correct.
